list.name: route
list.label: Route
list.query:
SELECT label || ' (' || ride_count || ' rides)' AS __text, id AS __value
FROM ride_routes
WHERE ride_count > 1
ORDER BY ride_count DESC, last_ridden DESC

panels.title: Route Summary
panels.description:
The selected route, summarised across every attempt.

Distance and elevation are medians, so one unusually long attempt does not skew them.

Shows no data until a route has been ridden at least twice — there is nothing to compare on a single attempt.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ride_count AS "Attempts",
       distance_m / 1000.0 AS "Distance (km)",
       elevation_m AS "Elevation (m)",
       first_ridden AS "First Ridden",
       last_ridden AS "Last Ridden"
FROM ride_routes
WHERE id = NULLIF('${route}', '')::integer

panels.title: Effort Trend
panels.description:
Effort on this route over time. Rising power at the same heart rate is fitness; a faster day at the same power is usually conditions.

Elapsed time is deliberately absent — on a stop-and-go route it mostly measures traffic lights.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT date AS time,
       np AS "NP (W)",
       avg_power AS "Avg Power (W)",
       avg_hr AS "Avg HR (bpm)"
FROM activities
WHERE route_id = NULLIF('${route}', '')::integer AND np IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY date

panels.title: Efficiency Trend
panels.description:
Efficiency Factor (NP / avg HR) rising while decoupling falls is the clearest aerobic-fitness signal available from stored data.

🟢 Decoupling < 5% — well within aerobic base

🟡 Decoupling 5-10% — moderate drift

🔴 Decoupling > 10% — significant drift

Rides under 20 minutes of pedalling store no decoupling value: heart-rate lag makes it meaningless over a short effort.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT date AS time,
       ef AS "Efficiency Factor",
       aerobic_decoupling AS "Aerobic Decoupling (%)"
FROM activities
WHERE route_id = NULLIF('${route}', '')::integer AND ef IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY date

panels.title: Latest vs Best vs Median
panels.description:
The most recent attempt against this route's best and median.

Median rather than mean, so a single exceptional ride does not move the reference.

targets.rawSql:
-- Each arm is parenthesised. An unparenthesised ORDER BY / LIMIT on a
-- UNION arm binds to the whole union and PostgreSQL rejects it.
(SELECT 'Latest' AS "Attempt", np AS "NP (W)", ef AS "EF"
 FROM activities WHERE route_id = NULLIF('${route}', '')::integer AND np IS NOT NULL
 ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 1)
UNION ALL
(SELECT 'Best', MAX(np), MAX(ef)
 FROM activities WHERE route_id = NULLIF('${route}', '')::integer AND np IS NOT NULL
 HAVING COUNT(*) > 0)
UNION ALL
(SELECT 'Median',
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY np),
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ef)
 FROM activities WHERE route_id = NULLIF('${route}', '')::integer AND np IS NOT NULL
 HAVING COUNT(*) > 0)

panels.title: Attempts
panels.description:
Every attempt on this route, newest first. Click a row to open that ride in Activity Details.

W/kg uses each ride's own stamped weight, so historical attempts keep the weight they were ridden at.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT date AS "Date",
       id AS "id",
       np AS "NP (W)",
       intensity_factor AS "IF",
       ef AS "EF",
       avg_hr AS "Avg HR",
       aerobic_decoupling AS "Decoupling (%)",
       tss AS "TSS",
       ROUND((np / NULLIF(ride_weight, 0))::numeric, 2) AS "W/kg",
       duration_s / 60 AS "Duration (min)",
       avg_speed_kmh AS "Avg Speed (km/h)",
       distance_m / 1000.0 AS "Distance (km)"
FROM activities
WHERE route_id = NULLIF('${route}', '')::integer
ORDER BY date DESC
